## Summary

Define Property

## Claim

### Prose Claim


The reusable lexical Term `Property` in Entity definitions, immediate-bearer
Relations, qualified Subject Paths, and authored content.


Property **means** an Entity whose identity depends on its immediate bearer and
whose direct bearer Relation is IS_PROPERTY_OF from that Property to the
bearer. This Claim explicitly introduces the lexical Term instance `Property`
at `Term//Property`.

## Semantics

The Term names the entity kind `Entity/Property`; it is not that entity kind
itself. `Property ((IS_PROPERTY_OF)) Bearer` states the direct Relation, and
`Bearer.Property` is its bearer-to-Property dot display. HAS_PROPERTY is the
strict derived inverse, not an independently stored reverse fact.

A bearer may itself be a Property, so a qualified expression such as
`bearer.property.status` remains permitted. This lexical meaning adds no generic lifecycle or update rule. The structural
Property Definition governs the approved acyclicity constraint on
IS_PROPERTY_OF, including self-loops. A Property is not another name for a YAML field; applicable
Delivery rules determine its representation.

## Details

Property is the sole canonical Term for this meaning. The R / Entity Definition
defines the `Entity/Property` kind, its immediate-bearer cardinality, no
separate Carrier, and direct-value Format/cardinality; this M / Term Definition
owns only the reusable lexical meaning. It introduces no separate Term group,
Terms Graph, projection, parser rule, runtime behavior, or Current-source
change.

The role-only Draft marker allocates no canonical Method identity. Adoption
requires the pending Entity root and Term governance declarations, the
structural Property definition, the Relation Definitions, and normal
identity/lifecycle checks. This Draft supplies no evidence that those effects
occurred.

## Summary

Define is derived relation of relation

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Relation//$relation ((IS_DERIVED_RELATION_OF)) Relation//$relation_2;

Relation//IS_DERIVED_RELATION_OF ((HAS_CLASSIFICATION)) Derivation == Direct
```

### Prose Claim

IS_DERIVED_RELATION_OF relates a derived Relation Type instance to its source Relation Type instance. It does not itself specify the endpoint transformation or any qualification. A direct Declaration's inverse binding entails the bound inverse's IS_DERIVED_RELATION_OF link to the direct Relation. This inferred metadata is not repeated in the minimal derived Declaration. A qualified derivation must retain its explicit qualification; it must not be normalized to an unconditional inverse. This Relation is distinct from DERIVED_FROM between Artifact Revisions.

## Summary

Define HAS_INVERSE

## Claim

### Formal Claim

```CFEL
# model
Relation//$relation ((HAS_INVERSE)) Relation//$relation_2;

alias(Relation//HAS_INVERSE) == "<-->";

Relation//HAS_INVERSE ((HAS_CLASSIFICATION)) Derivation == Direct
```

### Prose Claim

HAS_INVERSE binds a direct graph Relation to its derived inverse graph Relation. The Host is Direct and the Target is Derived. The inverse swaps Host and Target for each admitted direct fact. The two Relation identities remain distinct. The direct Declaration owns the shared meaning, endpoint signature, endpoint conditions and this binding; the derived Declaration supplies the reverse written counterpart binding and its own lexical alias when one exists. A bound inverse is inferred from the direct fact and is not authored separately. A qualified derived counterpart requires its qualification at the direct Declaration and is not an unconditional inverse.

`<-->` is the Subject notation alias for this binding. Written as `Relation//DIRECT <--> Relation//DERIVED` inside the direct Declaration, its left operand identifies the direct Relation and its right operand identifies the derived inverse. It is neither equality nor aliasing of the two Relation identities. The binding does not grant endpoint permissions or outgoing cardinalities.
